definitions.gloss: running away from home, leaving home (without permission)
definitions.explanation: Leaving one's home abruptly, especially as a young person fleeing family conflict or unhappiness. Can also apply to adults who abandon their household.

examples.japanese: {中学生|ちゅうがくせい}のとき{家出|いえで}をしたことがある。
examples.english: I ran away from home once when I was in middle school.

examples.japanese: {親|おや}と{喧嘩|けんか}して{家出|いえで}したが、{三日|みっか}で{帰|かえ}ってきた。
examples.english: I ran away from home after fighting with my parents, but I came back after three days.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly associated with teenagers or young people running away from home due to family problems. {家出|いえで}{少年|しょうねん}/{少女|しょうじょ} (runaway boy/girl) is a set phrase. The word carries a sense of impulsive departure rather than a planned move. It differs from simply moving out ({独立|どくりつ}する, {一人暮|ひとりぐ}らしを{始|はじ}める) in that {家出|いえで} implies leaving without approval or in conflict.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {家出|いえで}をする: to run away from home
- {家出|いえで}{少年|しょうねん}: runaway boy
- {家出|いえで}{少女|しょうじょ}: runaway girl
- {家出|いえで}{人|にん}: runaway, person who ran away from home
